A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 19-page versions of the same study. Their text, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison; appendix pages 11–19 are identical in text and rendering.

before.justification: v1 reports original native-speaker survey results and GPT-4o summarization experiments, including human evaluations, LLM evaluations and language-resource analyses in Sections 3–5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original survey and experimental results in Sections 3–5 and Appendix D. Their retention from v1 does not alter their empirical status.

M1.justification: The participatory guardrail-development process, iterative generator–verifier pipeline, human correction and guardrail-based summarization remain unchanged. The example guardrail and operational prompts in Appendices B and E are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same 42 languages and dialects and meeting-summarization task, with 27 languages selected for human evaluation. v2 describes scenario domains and replaces the illustrative hospital example with a product-launch example, without reporting additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Both versions compare GPT-4o summaries generated with and without language-specific guardrails. The English survey baseline and human-versus-LLM evaluation comparisons are also retained; no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 revises the reported curation conditions: v2 calls the 20 iterative outputs transcripts rather than verified transcripts and removes v1's explicit allowance for meaning loss during human correction. This is a limited documentation-level protocol revision, not evidence of rerunning experiments. Sample sizes, evaluation procedures, metrics and Appendix C call settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The qualitative guardrail analysis and comparison of human–LLM agreement across language-resource classes are retained with the same evidence. Section 5.2 changes its title from 'Language Availability' to 'Language Resources'; Figures 4–6 and the analysis itself are unchanged.

E5.justification: Uncertainty and agreement reporting are unchanged, including the survey average of 4.2 ± 0.3 and weighted human agreement of 0.75 ± 0.08. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval or statistical-testing information is added or removed.

E6.justification: Section 5.1 retains human-rated GA rates of 70% versus 24%, GM rates of 26% versus 14%, and quality scores of 1.7 versus 1.8 without versus with guardrails. All result plots are identical. Demographic percentages repeated in v2's Ethics section already appear in v1; the discussion qualification changes interpretation, not the underlying results.

T1.justification: The binary GA and GM definitions and three-level quality metric in Section 4.3 are unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions, proofs or formal derivations that differ between versions.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list newly present release of the guardrails, synthetic dataset and evaluation data as a contribution. v2 also explicitly describes the guardrails as reusable across applications. The central effectiveness and human–LLM disagreement claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 narrows effectiveness from 'all' to 'most' languages. Sections 7–8 add specific boundaries: deployment may increase misgendering, application-specific testing is needed, judge fine-tuning remains untested, and the guardrails do not address broader bias concerns. Evaluation on additional models and applications is identified as future work.

D1.justification: v1 uses anonymized placeholder links and promises a future release; v2 supplies a concrete repository reference and reports permissive release of the guardrails, synthetic transcripts and evaluation data. It also identifies the writing-style-guide source and adds resource-use instructions. This substantially changes documented access to core experimental materials, although repository contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works and bibliography are retained. The positioning as a first assessment at this scale involving native speakers is unchanged; identifying the existing style-guide source does not introduce a new research comparison.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized abstract, introduction, discussion and conclusion edits, expands the limitations and ethics paragraphs, and renames Section 5.2. It repeats existing demographic statistics in Ethics. The overall section order and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Added prose changes main-text column breaks and shifts the reference flow on pages 9–10. All 13 figures, both tables and six prompt panels retain their content and design; the appendix pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: Concrete resource references and release/use documentation improve reproducibility, while the 'most languages' discussion and specific deployment boundaries better qualify the unchanged evidence. The gain is limited: no experimental support is added, the abstract still generalizes effectiveness to all languages, and the explicit transcript-editing caveat about meaning loss is removed.
